```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(here); library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr)
library(ggplot2); library(scales); library(knitr)

processed  <- here("data","processed")
tbl_dir    <- here("output","tables")
fig_dir    <- here("output","figures")

pal <- c("Caribbean"="#0072B2","Pacific"="#D55E00","AIMS"="#009E73")

bl    <- read_csv(file.path(processed,"baseline_shock_recovery.csv"),show_col_types=FALSE)
cov   <- read_csv(file.path(processed,"country_coverage.csv"),       show_col_types=FALSE)
cands <- read_csv(file.path(processed,"candidates.csv"),              show_col_types=FALSE)
mres  <- read_csv(file.path(tbl_dir,"shock_model_results.csv"),       show_col_types=FALSE)
sens  <- read_csv(file.path(tbl_dir,"shock_sensitivity_restricted.csv"),show_col_types=FALSE)
rsum  <- read_csv(file.path(tbl_dir,"recovery_summary.csv"),          show_col_types=FALSE)
ridx  <- read_csv(file.path(processed,"recovery_index.csv"),           show_col_types=FALSE)
```

## Candidate Universe and Sample Definitions

```{r universe-summary}
#| echo: false
cands |>
  group_by(sids_region, sids_status) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups="drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from=sids_status, values_from=n, values_fill=0L) |>
  kable(caption="Table A1. Candidate universe: 58 economies across three SIDS regions. Authority: UN-OHRLLS list of SIDS, retrieved November 2026.")
```

### Three fixed samples

Sample membership is defined by 2017–2019 data availability and is **fixed** — it does not change when the baseline window is varied. Changes in N across specifications reflect only baseline-window coverage within a fixed set of countries.

```{r sample-counts}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Sample, ~Criterion, ~N,
  "Candidate universe", "All 58 economies", nrow(cands),
  "Tourism-data sample", "At least one tourism indicator, 2017-2019", sum(cov$in_tourism_data_sample),
  "OWID shock sample", "OWID vspend (2017-19) + 2020 GDP growth", sum(cov$in_primary_shock_sample),
  "WDI shock sample",  "WDI receipts (2017-19) + 2020 GDP growth", sum(cov$in_receipts_shock_sample),
  "Common sample",     "Both indicators (2017-19) + 2020 GDP growth", sum(cov$in_common_sample),
  "Recovery sample",   "OWID shock sample + real GDP (2019 + later year)", sum(cov$in_recovery_sample)
) |> kable(caption="Table A2. Sample definitions and sizes.")
```

**OWID-only economies** (in OWID shock sample but not common sample): `r paste(sort(setdiff(bl$iso3[bl$in_primary_shock_sample], bl$iso3[bl$in_common_sample])), collapse=", ")`.

**WDI-only economies** (in WDI shock sample but not common sample): `r paste(sort(setdiff(bl$iso3[bl$in_receipts_shock_sample], bl$iso3[bl$in_common_sample])), collapse=", ")`.

## Tourism Indicator Coverage

### Coverage matrix

```{r fig-coverage-matrix}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Data coverage matrix across the candidate universe. Green = all requested years available; yellow = partial; grey = absent."
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 10
knitr::include_graphics(here("output","figures","fig4_coverage_matrix.png"))
```

### WDI receipts publication lag

WDI `ST.INT.RCPT.XP.ZS` has **no observations beyond 2020** in the retrieved data. In 2019, 14 of 35 WDI sample members have no receipts observation — their 2017–2019 baseline is computed from 2017 and 2018 only. This lag distinguishes the WDI series from the OWID visitor spending series (available through 2024).

```{r wdi-coverage}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Indicator, ~`Latest year`, ~`2019 available?`, ~`Notes`,
  "OWID visitor spending (% GDP)", "2024", "Yes (all sample members)", "No lag; updated 2026",
  "WDI receipts (% exports)",      "2020", "14 of 35 missing",         "~3-5 year lag; absent 2021-2023+",
  "WDI real GDP (const. 2015 USD)","2024/2025", "Yes (all sample members)", "2025 preliminary for 22/29"
) |> kable(caption="Table A3. Key coverage differences between tourism indicators.")
```

### Baseline coverage distributions

```{r baseline-coverage}
#| echo: false
samples_list <- list(
  "OWID (N=29)" = bl |> filter(in_primary_shock_sample),
  "WDI (N=35)"  = bl |> filter(in_receipts_shock_sample),
  "Common (N=24)"= bl |> filter(in_common_sample)
)
purrr::map_dfr(names(samples_list), function(nm) {
  d <- samples_list[[nm]]
  tibble(
    Sample = nm,
    Indicator = c("OWID vspend","OWID vspend","WDI receipts","WDI receipts"),
    Window    = c("2015-19","2017-19","2015-19","2017-19"),
    `0 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==0), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==0),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==0), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==0)),
    `1 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==1), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==1),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==1), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==1)),
    `2 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==2), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==2),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==2), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==2)),
    `3 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==3), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==3),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==3), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==3)),
    `4 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==4), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==4),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==4), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==4)),
    `5 obs`   = c(sum(d$vspend_n_1519==5), sum(d$vspend_n_1719==5),
                  sum(d$receipts_n_1519==5), sum(d$receipts_n_1719==5))
  )
}) |>
  kable(caption=paste0("Table A4. Annual observation counts within each baseline window, ",
                       "restricted to fixed sample members. WDI receipts 2017-19 window has ",
                       "many economies with only 2 observations (2017+2018) because 2019 data ",
                       "is missing from the WDI series."))
```

## Indicator Comparison

```{r fig-indicator-comparison}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "OWID visitor spending (% GDP) vs. WDI tourism receipts (% exports), 2015–2019 averages. The two indicators are correlated but not interchangeable — they divide by different denominators and measure related but distinct economic concepts."
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 6
knitr::include_graphics(here("output","figures","fig2_measure_comparison.png"))
```

The Pearson correlation between the two indicators (across economies with both) is approximately 0.77, and the Spearman rank correlation is 0.86. They produce similar rankings but material differences for some economies. The WDI receipts/exports denominator amplifies the apparent dependence of export-intensive small economies, while the OWID visitor spending/GDP denominator captures the share of overall economic activity attributable to visitors.

## Eight-Model Shock Analysis

**Outcome:** 2020 annual GDP growth (%, WDI `NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG`).  
**Note:** The 2015–2019 primary window was evaluated after the 2017–2019 results were already observed. No window was designated a priori. All eight results are reported.

```{r full-results}
#| echo: false
mres |>
  mutate(`95% CI` = paste0("[",CI_lo,", ",CI_hi,"]")) |>
  select(Model, Indicator, Window, Sample, N, Slope, `95% CI`, R2,
         Pearson_r, Spearman_rho, p_raw, p_holm) |>
  kable(digits=3,
        caption=paste0("Table A5. Complete eight-model results. Holm correction applied ",
                       "across all 8 raw p-values. No result is suppressed."))
```

#| echo: false

#| fig-width: 13

knitr::include_graphics(here("output","figures","fig5_shock_4panel_1519.png"))

### Influential observations

```{r influential}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Model, ~`Most influential`, ~`Cook's D`, ~`Slope (orig.)`, ~`Slope (excl.)`, ~`R² (orig.)`, ~`R² (excl.)`, ~`p (excl.)`,
  "M1 OWID/2015-19/OWID (N=29)",    "MDV", "0.392", "-0.308", "-0.251", "0.414", "0.309", "0.002",
  "M2 WDI/2015-19/WDI (N=35)",      "TLS", "0.287", "-0.120", "-0.141", "0.100", "0.224", "0.005",
  "M3 OWID/2015-19/Common (N=24)",   "MDV", "0.363", "-0.331", "-0.276", "0.489", "0.389", "0.002",
  "M4 WDI/2015-19/Common (N=24)",    "MDV", "0.339", "-0.158", "-0.116", "0.233", "0.157", "0.062",
  "M5 OWID/2017-19/OWID (N=29)",    "MDV", "0.384", "-0.320", "-0.263", "0.428", "0.331", "0.001",
  "M6 WDI/2017-19/WDI (N=35)",      "TLS", "0.324", "-0.116", "-0.142", "0.097", "0.234", "0.004",
  "M7 OWID/2017-19/Common (N=24)",   "MDV", "0.362", "-0.339", "-0.284", "0.493", "0.402", "0.001",
  "M8 WDI/2017-19/Common (N=24)",    "MDV", "0.334", "-0.160", "-0.120", "0.248", "0.173", "0.048"
) |> kable(caption=paste0("Table A6. Most influential observation per model (Cook's D threshold = 4/N). ",
           "MDV = Maldives; TLS = Timor-Leste. The OWID association ",
           "survives MDV exclusion; the WDI/TLS exclusion actually strengthens M2 and M6."))
```

**Why Timor-Leste influences M2 and M6:** Timor-Leste has moderately high WDI tourism receipts as a share of exports but experienced a modest 2020 contraction, making it a structural outlier in the WDI receipts models. Excluding it makes those models stronger, not weaker — a counter-intuitive diagnostic result worth noting.

## Recovery Analysis

### Coverage

```{r recovery-coverage}
#| echo: false
ridx |>
  filter(!is.na(gdp_index)) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(`N with real GDP` = n()) |>
  kable(caption="Table A8. Annual count of primary shock sample economies (N ≤ 29) with real GDP data. 2025 data are preliminary estimates.")
```

### Trajectories

```{r fig-recovery-trajectories}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Real GDP recovery trajectories, 2015–2025 (index: 2019=100). Line colour = SIDS region. Bottom numbers = annual sample size."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 10
knitr::include_graphics(here("output","figures","fig7_recovery_trajectories.png"))
```

### Recovery status by 2023

```{r recovery-table}
#| echo: false
# Per-capita columns are in the baseline dataset, not recovery_summary
pcap_data <- bl |>
  filter(in_primary_shock_sample) |>
  mutate(
    gdppc_idx_2023 = gdppc_real_const2015usd_2023 / gdppc_real_const2015usd_2019 * 100
  ) |>
  select(iso3, gdppc_idx_2023)

rsum |>
  left_join(pcap_data, by="iso3") |>
  select(iso3, label, sids_region, shock_2020, gdp_idx_2023, gdppc_idx_2023,
         recovered_by_2023) |>
  mutate(across(c(shock_2020, gdp_idx_2023, gdppc_idx_2023), ~round(., 1))) |>
  arrange(sids_region, iso3) |>
  kable(col.names=c("ISO3","Economy","Region","2020<br>(shock)","GDP idx<br>2023","GDP/cap<br>idx 2023","Agg.<br>recovered"),
        caption=paste0("Table A9. Aggregate real GDP and per-capita real GDP recovery indices ",
               "(2019=100). 'Agg. recovered' = GDP ≥ 100 in 2023. VIR has no 2023 data. ",
               "19/28 recovered aggregate GDP by 2023; 17/28 recovered per-capita GDP by 2023. Four economies (COM, SYC, PNG, VUT) recovered aggregate but not per-capita; two (MHL, PRI) recovered per-capita but not aggregate.."), escape=FALSE)
```

### Recovery vs. tourism dependence

```{r fig-recovery-vs-tourism}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Pre-pandemic visitor spending vs. 2023 real GDP index (2019=100). No statistically significant association (Pearson r = 0.18, p = 0.36, N = 28). Tourism-dependent economies had both the worst shocks and the strongest recoveries."
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 6
knitr::include_graphics(here("output","figures","fig8_recovery_vs_tourism.png"))
```

The absence of a significant association between tourism dependence and the 2023 recovery index (Figure 6) is **not** evidence that tourism dependence is harmless or that the shock was ultimately irrelevant. It reflects the fact that the same sectors that collapsed in 2020 — international tourism and hospitality — were also the sectors that recovered as travel rebounded. Economies with high visitor spending contracted sharply in 2020 and rebounded sharply from 2021 onward, producing a near-symmetrical pattern in aggregate GDP terms.

Per-capita recovery tells a more nuanced story: 17 of 28 economies had recovered GDP per person by 2023, compared with 19 of 28 for aggregate GDP. The 2-economy gap reflects continued population growth in some Pacific economies, where total output recovered but output per person had not yet returned to 2019 levels.
